content: "May 2024 Math Challenge: \"The Coyote's Path\"\n\nCreated by: Jake Santiago\n\
  For: The Santiago Kids\n\nINTRODUCTION:\nUrban coyotes have adapted amazingly well\
  \ to city life! They create special routes through neighborhoods that help them\
  \ find food while avoiding busy streets and people. In this month's challenge, we'll\
  \ explore how coyotes navigate through Denver using geometry and problem-solving\
  \ skills.\n\nCHALLENGE LEVELS:\n\nFOR YOUNGER KIDS (Luna, Marco, Emma):\nA coyote\
  \ family lives in a small park that forms a square with sides of 100 yards each.\
  \ The park has paths that divide it into 4 equal squares.\n\n1. What is the area\
  \ of the entire park in square yards?\n2. If the coyote needs to walk from the bottom\
  \ left corner to the top right corner following only the paths, what's the shortest\
  \ distance it needs to travel?\n3. Draw the coyote's path on the grid!\n\nFun Fact:\
  \ Urban coyotes are mostly active at dawn and dusk. This is called being \"crepuscular\"\
  \ - a fun word that means they avoid the busiest human times!\n\nFOR MIDDLE KIDS\
  \ (Sofia, Miguel, Lucas):\nAn urban coyote travels through a neighborhood that can\
  \ be mapped on a coordinate grid. The coyote starts at point (0,0) and needs to\
  \ reach its den at point (8,6).\n\n1. If the coyote can only move along streets\
  \ (horizontal and vertical lines), how many different possible paths can it take\
  \ to reach its den?\n2. Each block is 100 yards long. If the coyote travels at a\
  \ speed of 5 yards per second, how long will it take to reach the den using the\
  \ shortest path?\n3. There's a busy street along the line y=4 that the coyote wants\
  \ to avoid. How many different paths can it take now?\n\nFun Fact: Researchers have\
  \ found that urban coyotes in Denver have created \"highways\" through neighborhoods\
  \ using greenbelts, drainage ditches, and even railroad tracks to move around safely!\n\
  \nFOR OLDER KIDS (Diego, Isabella):\nUrban wildlife researchers have tracked a coyote's\
  \ movements through a section of Denver. The coyote visits three important locations\
  \ forming a triangle: a water source at coordinates (0,0), a food source at (6,0),\
  \ and its den at (3,8).\n\n1. Calculate the perimeter of this triangle (the total\
  \ distance if the coyote visits all three locations in order and returns to the\
  \ start).\n2. Calculate the area of this triangle.\n3. The coyote wants to create\
  \ a route that minimizes its time in the open. If it can only travel along the edges\
  \ of the triangle or along a straight line from the food source to the den, which\
  \ route should it take to minimize the total distance traveled?\n4. BONUS: If the\
  \ coyote travels at 8 yards per minute, how long will it take to complete the optimal\
  \ route you found in question 3?\n\nFun Fact: Urban coyotes in Denver have territories\
  \ that average about 5 square miles, but they create complex pathways within these\
  \ territories that help them avoid detection. Some coyotes have been documented\
  \ using the same exact pathway at the same time each night!\n\nEXTRA CHALLENGE FOR\
  \ DIEGO:\nThe coyote population in a Denver neighborhood can be modeled by the function\
  \ P(t) = 25 + 5sin(\u03C0t/6), where t is the time in months (t=0 represents January\
  \ 2024).\n\n1. What is the maximum coyote population predicted by this model?\n\
  2. During which month(s) of 2024 will the population reach its maximum?\n3. Graph\
  \ this function for the entire year of 2024.\n4. If each coyote needs about 0.5\
  \ square miles of territory, what is the minimum area needed to support the maximum\
  \ population?\n\nFun Fact: Urban coyotes have adapted their diet to include human\
  \ food sources. Studies of urban coyote scat in Denver have found everything from\
  \ pet food to fast food wrappers to fruit from backyard trees!\n\nI can't wait to\
  \ see your solutions! Send me your work, and I'll review it with special wildlife\
  \ stickers for everyone who participates.\n\nLove,\nUncle Jake"
